scenes.heading: Analyzing a rental property before buying

sents.d: Analyzing a rental property before buying
Running real numbers prevents an emotionally appealing property from becoming a bad investment.

A basic rental analysis compares expected monthly rental income against all expenses — mortgage payment, property taxes, insurance, maintenance reserves, property management if applicable, and vacancy allowance — not just the mortgage payment alone.

Common quick screening metrics like the 1% rule (monthly rent should be roughly 1% of purchase price) can help filter properties worth deeper analysis, though they're rough guides, not guarantees of profitability in every market.

Being conservative in estimates — assuming some vacancy, real maintenance costs, and not the best-case rent — protects against the common mistake of an overly optimistic analysis that looks profitable on paper but isn't in practice.

take: Analyze rentals with every expense and conservative numbers.
